Before a new invocation, the runner performs another exact observation and requires running status, no cancellation, the same current attempt/owner/epoch and an unexpired grant. It creates wire attempt correlation deterministically from the issued UUID while preserving the accepted logical fingerprint.

This avoids accidental re-execution after a coordinator crash between issuance and transport. It deliberately leaves a gap where an issued attempt may never have called the specialist. Recovery requires a separately supplied new command after P1 decides a new issuance is eligible. That trade-off preserves clear authority and uncertainty without claiming a universal one-computation guarantee.

followups.question: Why not invoke after finding an ambiguously issued grant?
followups.answer: Finding a grant proves issuance, not whether the original caller sent HTTP. Reinvocation could duplicate an already-running computation. The current contract makes replay lookup-only and requires an explicit fresh eligible issuance for another invocation.

followups.question: Does the HTTP server independently verify the P1 grant?
followups.answer: In this wire version it authenticates its own local service principal and validates the bounded attempt contract. It does not independently query P1 issuance. The issued-execution guarantee belongs to the trusted runner path, not arbitrary direct HTTP callers.

questions.watch_for: Never equate a proposed attempt ID with issued execution permission, or advertise exactly-once computation.

evidence.label: Observe, issue and created-only invocation schedule
Replay and fresh grant checks before HTTP

questions.title: Bound the entire HTTP lifecycle
questions.question: Where are the resource limits, and why is a semaphore around model invocation insufficient?
answer: The TypeScript service separately caps connections, in-flight requests, active invocations, per-principal invocations, header bytes/fields, header time, body time, invoke time, response time and close time. Defaults include sixteen connections/requests, four active attempts and two per principal; these are configured ceilings rather than measured production capacity. The bounded parser admits only explicit POST endpoints and validates framing before capability handling.

An invocation semaphore alone leaves slow headers, oversized bodies, response backpressure, open sockets, decoding and cleanup unbounded. P3 reserves and observes each relevant lifetime, translates failures to fixed safe codes and starts no listener merely because a module is imported. The document capability adds its own finite workers and provider ownership inside the same authenticated transport boundary.

On timeout, disconnect or close, the server asks cooperative work to abort while retaining ownership until evaluation settles. This is essential for a real capacity bound: returning a 504 cannot free memory or provider work that still runs. A production extension would measure each layer under adversarial slow peers and declare admission behavior under saturation instead of treating these small local defaults as a scale benchmark.

followups.question: Why cap requests separately from connections?
followups.answer: Connection and request lifetimes differ, and a request may retain body, handler or response resources even when invocation never starts. Independent bounds make the maximum outstanding parser and application state explicit rather than relying on one downstream semaphore.

followups.question: What should happen at capacity?
followups.answer: Reject before starting new expensive work with a fixed capacity signal, while retaining the occupied slots until actual settlement. The caller may retry only under its own explicit identity and eligibility contract; the server must not silently create a recovering queue.

questions.watch_for: A bounded active map does not by itself bound TCP, parse buffers, decoder memory, responses or cleanup.

evidence.label: Permit, deadline, disconnect and abort ownership

questions.title: Cancellation stops a waiter first
questions.question: What happens when the LiveKit SDK cancels a tool that is waiting for delegated work?
answer: P3 treats waiter cancellation, business cancellation and remote cooperation as separate events. The coordinator creates an owned task and shields it from cancellation of the external waiter. A timed-out write returns acknowledgement_unknown; a timed-out preflight returns a deadline error and marks abandonment so it cannot start a later write. Actual I/O retains its slot until its done callback observes settlement.

NativePolicyApplication follows the same principle. After durable acceptance it owns one runner task, publishes pending progress and shields the actual run. SDK cancellation changes tool_waiter to stopped_waiting without cancelling accepted work or freeing its occupied run slot. Repeated calls inspect the original configured identity. A separate explicit coordinator cancel command records business cancellation through P1; a remote cancel response is only an observation about cooperation.

This gives a conversation permission to remain responsive without inventing a guarantee that HTTP or a provider stopped. Tests hold actual operations past wrapper timeout and verify that replacement work is rejected until settlement. Closing can report cleanup_incomplete, preserving ownership for an explicit later observation rather than discarding a still-live task.

followups.question: Why not let asyncio cancellation propagate everywhere?
followups.answer: It should propagate to the caller, but cancellation of the caller cannot undo a database commit or prove a thread or remote request stopped. Owned external operations require a retained observer, and preflight abandonment checks prevent starting new authority-changing work after the caller leaves.

followups.question: What should the user hear after interruption?
followups.answer: A truthful statement that the agent stopped waiting or speaking, with the original work still pending or unknown when applicable. The interface can inspect or explicitly request business cancellation; interruption itself should not be reported as cancellation success.

questions.watch_for: CancelledError, timeout and a non-durable remote ACK do not mean the business operation was prevented.

evidence.label: Shielded ownership and phase-sensitive timeout result
Native accepted task and waiter cancellation
SDK waiter cancellation retains actual ownership

questions.title: Separate the clocks and deadlines
questions.question: How would you explain the project's deadline model under clock skew and late network responses?
answer: There are several clocks with different jobs. Event-loop monotonic deadlines bound local waits and cleanup. Wire epoch deadlines bind the accepted request's business horizon. P1 evaluates issuance/result eligibility with its authoritative database-time and lease/cancellation state. Producer completed_at metadata is correlation and provenance; it cannot overrule P1's eligibility decision.

The runner rechecks the current issued grant before starting HTTP and sends the original request deadline. Once computation starts, it may return after expiry, cancellation or supersession. A structurally and factually valid late result can still be recorded as history with an ineligible disposition. An eligible result already committed remains a historical fact after the old grant lease later expires; applicability and new delivery/action permission are evaluated separately.

The deadline gate uses an explicitly test-only noncooperating peer and reads real P1 database time after admission. This avoids changing production cooperation merely to make a fault schedule pass. It distinguishes deadline-before-issue, expiry-before-HTTP and expiry-during-HTTP. In a production design, document clock assumptions and skew allowances explicitly, and avoid presenting host-time display observations as atomic database eligibility.

followups.question: The specialist says it completed before the deadline. Can we use it?
followups.answer: That timestamp is insufficient. Validate the result and inspect its P1 commit disposition, current work/case applicability and the permission for the intended next operation. A producer can be skewed or untrusted, and network delay may place the commit outside authority eligibility.

followups.question: Does lease expiry delete a result?
followups.answer: No. Lease expiry limits an attempt owner and may affect a new completion disposition. It does not erase a previously recorded eligible result or original receipt. Later action or delivery still needs its own fresh admission checks.

questions.watch_for: Do not use producer timestamps to grant eligibility or confuse local wait budgets with the accepted business deadline.

evidence.label: Fresh exact grant checks before invocation
Historical disposition remains part of result truth

questions.title: Truth and applicability are different
questions.question: A result is valid and says the customer is eligible. Why might it still be unusable?
answer: A result can be valid for its immutable request while no longer applying to the current case. The runner first validates scope, request/result correlation, canonical bytes and factual evidence. P1 separately records whether the result was eligible_at_commit with respect to execution time, lease and cancellation. Neither check means the customer's current request still matches that result.

The read view therefore derives applicability. It distinguishes missing, candidate, clarification, outdated, case_cancelled, expired, execution_ineligible and unavailable. It reads the public case adapter separately and compares the observed request revision to the immutable request revision. If the case read is foreign, malformed or unavailable, it returns unavailable without inventing current authority. The answer remains an explicitly timed observation rather than an atomic snapshot spanning every authority.

For example, result A may correctly evaluate a ten-day notice request. If the user revises to request B with three days' notice, A remains true history about A and cannot authorize B. The useful-progress requirement is equally important: separately accepted, current B must still be able to complete and, where supported, proceed through separately confirmed exact action guards.

followups.question: Can a cached green candidate badge authorize an action?
followups.answer: No. It is derived as-of metadata and may become stale without a new result-feed event. The final action boundary must atomically revalidate current case revision, exact human confirmation and the applicable work/result conditions.

followups.question: How do you explain unavailable versus invalid?
followups.answer: Unavailable means a dependency prevented establishing a fact now. Invalid means the received identity, schema or evidence demonstrably violates the contract. Treating a transient read failure as corrupt source state can block useful later processing and mislead operators.

questions.watch_for: eligible_at_commit is time/lease/cancellation eligibility, not semantic correctness, current applicability or consent.

evidence.label: Strict read view and separately timed applicability
Current cancellation, fact time and case revision branches

questions.title: Verify facts after parsing
questions.question: How does fixed-policy v2 catch a schema-valid but factually wrong specialist response?
answer: The fixed-policy verifier loads the exact scoped policy and fact records named by the accepted request. Each reference carries source identity, version, digest, media type and byte length. It rejects duplicate or mismatched source records, validates the fixed policy version/rule/threshold, and reconstructs the expected fact witnesses from the immutable facts document.

It then compares the response's rule and fact references to those expected values and recomputes the answer. The current synthetic rule is a minimum seven days' notice. No observations means missing uncertainty; distinct conflicting observed values mean conflicting uncertainty; one supported value means an eligible boolean determined by the fixed threshold. A response with plausible citations but the wrong boolean is unsupported_facts rather than a trusted result.

This is intentionally narrow deterministic verification, not general truth verification for arbitrary LLM prose. The important engineering feature is that factual validation remains independent of transport and structure, and is performed even for late historical responses. The audit corrected TypeScript parity so expiry cannot short-circuit detection of a factually wrong response. A late wrong answer must not enter history as if only timing were wrong.

followups.question: Why verify an already expired response?
followups.answer: Historical data is still consumed by inspection, reconciliation and debugging. Marking wrong facts merely expired would preserve a misleading record and create cross-language differences. First establish the exact supported content, then classify its timeliness and permitted uses.

followups.question: Does deterministic verification make the model unnecessary?
followups.answer: For this fixed arithmetic rule, deterministic execution is appropriate and intentionally testable. The framework still demonstrates evidence and ownership boundaries needed for richer specialists. Do not add an LLM where a reliable small function already expresses the business rule.

questions.watch_for: A valid schema and a citation-shaped object do not establish source support; expiry is not permission to skip validation.

questions.title: Keep uncertainty useful
questions.question: Why do missing or conflicting source facts produce clarification instead of eligible=false?
answer: False and unknown mean different things. False says the supported facts establish ineligibility under the fixed rule. Missing or conflicting observations cannot establish either eligibility or ineligibility. Fixed-policy results therefore carry eligible=null together with explicit missing or conflicting uncertainty and the exact relevant witnesses.

The source verifier derives uncertainty from the retained observations rather than trusting the specialist's label. No distinct values means missing; one distinct value supports a definite calculation; two different values require clarification. Both languages verify that the result's boolean/null state and witness list agree with that derivation. The result can remain a valid clarification outcome instead of becoming a generic transport failure.

This improves both user experience and safety. The conversational agent can ask for the missing booking detail while the original evidence remains inspectable. It must not select the convenient value, average conflicting dates or treat a model confidence score as confirmation. The exact guarded action path requires a definite supported eligible result and separate human confirmation, so clarification is useful progress without becoming mutation authority.

followups.question: Can duplicate observations agree?
followups.answer: Agreement of retained observations can support one distinct value if the exact contract permits those witnesses and their identities are unique. It still does not prove the underlying real world is correct; the claim is only about the fixed trusted synthetic source records supplied to this calculation.

followups.question: What do you store when the user clarifies?
followups.answer: A new accepted input or explicitly versioned current case revision, with a fresh immutable work request where appropriate. Preserve the old conflicting result as history rather than editing its facts to make a previous command appear successful.

questions.watch_for: Do not collapse unknown into negative, or let a confidence score authorize a booking change.

evidence.label: Expected fact references and uncertainty derivation

questions.title: Do not retarget a result
questions.question: How does result delivery remain bound to the original receiver and recipient?
answer: Delivery is a separate explicit facade over P1's delivery authority and a cooperating receiver. Trusted construction fixes receiver identity and finite case/conversation-to-recipient bindings. Before preparing new delivery, the facade validates the full original request/result/evidence and requires current eligibility. P1 records an immutable intent containing work, issued attempt, result digest, receiver and recipient.

Only a newly created begin marker permits receiver.accept. The marker means the external accept call may have happened, so a repeated possible delivery performs receiver.find only. A known receipt is validated against every original field and recorded back in P1. Changing current channel configuration cannot silently send those original bytes to another receiver or recipient, even if the new route looks more convenient.

The design distinguishes accepted result bytes, P2/carrier delivery, browser playback and human acknowledgement. A receiver receipt establishes only its own acceptance contract. The v2 and origin-bound delivery facades extend supported result schemas explicitly while retaining this stable-receiver rule. That protects replay semantics through case changes and restarts, but it deliberately does not guarantee eventual delivery when a possible call remains unresolved.

followups.question: What if the original recipient changes phone number?
followups.answer: A possible delivery remains bound to its original receiver/recipient intent and must be reconciled there. A new logical operation with explicit current permission is a separate design decision; changing configuration must not rewrite the history of a possibly executed send.

followups.question: Why find before accept on a new begin?
followups.answer: It allows reconciliation with a cooperating receiver that already has the exact receipt, while preserving one immutable delivery identity. If no receipt is found, only the call that actually created begin may accept. Other callers remain lookup-only.

questions.watch_for: Receiver acceptance is not carrier delivery, audible playback or human acknowledgement.

questions.title: Explain a permanently unknown send
questions.question: If a possible delivery has no receiver receipt after restart, why not retry accept?
answer: A possible-send marker commits before receiver I/O. After a crash, receipt absence cannot prove the receiver never accepted: the call may still be in flight, a receipt may not yet be visible, or its acknowledgement may have been lost. The current policy therefore keeps existing possible delivery lookup-only. It does not convert reliable absence into a new accept authorization.

The facade can recover a matching known receipt and persist it without calling accept again. If none is found, it returns unknown. Later cancellation, expiry or case revision does not transform that old uncertainty into a definite not-delivered outcome, nor permit a terminal skip of the event. This is a deliberate availability trade-off for explicit effect safety at a boundary without a stronger remote protocol.

Useful later work must still progress. The completion processor scans around unresolved events while leaving them unACKed and retaining a contiguous terminal watermark behind the gap. A future stronger policy could use a cooperating idempotent operation contract or authoritative remote nonacceptance witness, but it would need explicit persisted semantics and new qualification. It must not be inferred from a timeout or an empty lookup.

followups.question: Is this at-most-once delivery?
followups.answer: The facade permits one accept call per newly created begin under its contract and lookup-only replay, but it does not establish a universal transport delivery guarantee. The receiver may have accepted despite uncertainty, and external implementation behavior still matters.

followups.question: How would operations resolve the unknown?
followups.answer: Expose the immutable work/attempt/result/receiver/recipient identity, observe the original receiver and retain evidence. An operator may need a separately designed remediation operation; the system should not clear the marker or retarget it merely to make the dashboard look complete.

questions.watch_for: Absence is not a receipt of nonacceptance; a terminal ACK must not erase possible external work.

evidence.label: Absent original receipt retains unknown without accept
Known receipt precedes fresh applicability policy

questions.title: Commit an action atomically
questions.question: Why can't the coordinator read candidate status and then call a plain case mutation API?
answer: A read-then-mutate sequence has a race: case revision, cancellation, result eligibility or the selected attempt can change after the read. P3's DelegationAuthorizer performs strict preflight validation but sends the actual command through P1's public ActionPort, which guards work/result eligibility and exact case authority in one protected transaction on the same PostgreSQL target.

The caller supplies a separate exact Confirmation. It is defensively copied before the first await and must bind the expected task, authority case and request revision. The result must be definitely eligible with no uncertainty. P1 then validates the current revision and exact confirmation and records both the action receipt and case intent together. Supplier I/O occurs later in the existing leased worker, outside the SQL transaction.

An ambiguous authorization commit is reconciled by its original command identity; a matching original receipt remains a fact after later expiry or cancellation. The current action adapter is explicitly the original supported v1 path. Do not assume fixed-policy v2 or origin-bound v3 delivery support automatically grants those schemas projection or action capability.

followups.question: The model says the customer confirmed. Is that enough?
followups.answer: No. Model output, playback and correlation IDs grant no mutation authority. Exact human confirmation is supplied through the authenticated controller boundary and validated by the case authority against the trusted quote and revision.

followups.question: What if action commit succeeds but the reply is lost?
followups.answer: Read the original action command receipt and verify all bindings, including exact confirmation. Do not create a replacement command or call the supplier directly. The durable intent already governs downstream execution and reconciliation.

questions.watch_for: Preflight applicability is not the action commitment point; v2/v3 delivery support is not v2/v3 action support.

evidence.label: Separate copied confirmation and exact authorization
One original-action lookup after uncertain commit

questions.title: Defend both action race outcomes
questions.question: A user revises request A to B while A is being authorized. What outcomes are correct?
answer: There are two correct serialized outcomes, determined by the authoritative transaction order. If revision B commits first, A's expected-revision guard rejects the stale action. A separate current B result and newly confirmed exact B quote may still progress. If A's intent commits first, B's revision must reject with intent_committed; a later edit cannot silently undo an already committed action intent.

The race gate exercises real PostgreSQL lock waits instead of relying on sleeps. It prewarms both writers, observes two admission waiters and actual pg_blocking_pids chains, and releases them in both orders. It also distinguishes cancellation before commitment/dispatch, cancellation after a supplier reservation and known terminal success. Those cuts require different outcomes because a database fence cannot stop an already admitted external request.

The proof joins authoritative action receipts, original confirmations, retained cancellations and independent supplier identities. Counting only deduplicated supplier successes is insufficient: two physical apply calls might have occurred even if the supplier exposes one logical effect. The frozen gate therefore inspects every apply call and uses owned process kills at explicit commit boundaries, preserving both safety and useful current progress.

followups.question: Why not let B always win because its timestamp is newer?
followups.answer: Timestamp order is not transaction arbitration and cannot rewrite an intent that already committed. The actual protected authority serializes the conflicting commands. If the product needs compensation after commitment, that is an explicit new business workflow with its own consent and external-effect semantics.

followups.question: Why prove a real lock waiter graph?
followups.answer: A test that merely launches two tasks may execute them sequentially and miss the race entirely. Observing the real backend blocker chain demonstrates that both writers reached the intended contention boundary before choosing the order.

questions.watch_for: Do not promise that a later revision or cancellation can revoke an already admitted supplier call.

evidence.label: Frozen race modes and explicit barriers

questions.title: Project references without cloning authority
questions.question: Why does the P3 result projector store references and as-of metadata instead of complete result blobs?
answer: P1's result feed owns stable source identity, scoped sequence and immutable result events. The P3 projector validates that an event matches the original issuance and historical result, then stores bounded reference metadata together with a checkpoint. It does not copy accepted work into a second scheduler or create a new source acknowledgement API.

The projector distinguishes definite invalid P3 content from unavailable or corrupt source state. A well-bound source event containing definitely unsupported P3 bytes can become rejected metadata, allowing later progress. Missing historical issuance, mismatched result digest or unavailable authority cannot advance the checkpoint because the projector has not established the source event's meaning. A possible projection commit permits one exact reconciliation read, never an automatic second apply.

Applicability stored here is immutable as_of_non_atomic metadata, with separately observed execution and case fields. A case-only revision can invalidate it without producing another result event, which is why later refresh is explicit. The current original projector uses v1 codecs; the latest audit records that v2/v3 policy events are quarantined by that path. Extending projection semantics requires an explicit reviewed version change, not claiming all result schemas already flow through it.

followups.question: Can we rebuild the projection?
followups.answer: It is derived, but rebuilding must still preserve the explicit source incarnation, scoped cursor and protected command/receipt identities according to its lifecycle contract. A casual truncate-and-replay can destroy retained ACK or display semantics and is not authorized by calling the data derived.

followups.question: Why no result blob in P3?
followups.answer: Keeping the authoritative bytes in P1 prevents two stores from disagreeing about original result truth. P3 retains digests and identities sufficient to verify its observations, then reads the public authority when it needs the exact historical body.

questions.watch_for: Derived does not mean disposable; v1 projection support must not be advertised as v2/v3 compatibility.

evidence.label: Event, issuance and exact historical result join
V1 codec validation and definite rejection

questions.title: Scan around unresolved work
questions.question: Why does completion processing need both scan_after and a terminal watermark?
answer: A single cursor cannot represent both discovery progress and proof that every earlier event is finished. P3 therefore separates scan_after, which chooses what to inspect next, from the contiguous terminal watermark, which advances only over immutable terminal processing ACKs. An unknown delivery remains a gap in terminal progress while later useful events can still be discovered and processed.

Each explicit step examines at most eight unACKed references total. The store performs at most two page queries with one wrap, using only the remaining budget on the second query. This avoids the common bug of fetching eight new rows plus eight wrapped rows while claiming an eight-row bound. Source/work/attempt/request/result/receiver/recipient bindings are checked before a new ACK can consume an event.

An existing known receiver receipt is reconciled before fresh applicability, because receipt truth survives later cancellation. An unresolved possible send remains unACKed. An event outside frozen route bindings is counted unroutable and remains unACKed, while discovery advances around it. Processing ACKs describe completion of this local delivery policy; they are not P1 source ACKs, execution results, action permission or human acknowledgement.

followups.question: Can the terminal watermark move past a gap?
followups.answer: No. Individual later events may have terminal ACKs, but the contiguous watermark must stop immediately before the first unACKed event. Discovery can move ahead independently and wrap once to revisit unresolved rows within the same finite examination budget.

followups.question: What about a new case with no configured recipient?
followups.answer: The frozen policy cannot silently invent or retarget a recipient. That row stays unroutable and unACKed; later bound rows should progress. Updating the route policy requires an explicit lifecycle decision rather than mutating an original possible delivery.

questions.watch_for: A scan cursor is not an ACK watermark, and a local processing ACK is not a source or human acknowledgement.

evidence.label: Two queries and one wrap share the same total limit
Unroutable gap and known receipt handling

questions.title: Keep transient errors from blocking progress
questions.question: How does the latest completion processor handle a temporarily unavailable dependency?
answer: The processor distinguishes availability failures from definite identity or authorization violations. Fixed transient codes such as storage_unavailable, capacity, deadline_exceeded and cleanup_incomplete map to a per-row unavailable outcome. The row receives no terminal ACK, but the bounded scan can continue to later work. A forged source or contradictory immutable result still fails closed.

This behavior fixes an audit finding where transient dependency failures appeared as invalid_source_state and aborted the whole processing step. It also preserves uncertainty: acknowledgement_unknown during delivery remains unknown, not a terminal failure or permission to resend. The processor's metrics count unavailable, unknown and unroutable observations separately from acknowledged events.

Close is observed between rows. If close arrives while the first row commits, the processor retains that actual commit and prevents a new later row from starting. This is a useful example of lifecycle semantics beyond a broad try/finally: the first effect may be real even though the overall step was interrupted. Tests therefore need to assert both the retained first-row truth and zero unauthorized later-row work.

followups.question: Why not ACK unavailable as a terminal error?
followups.answer: Unavailable describes what this observation could establish, not the source event's final disposition. Terminally ACKing it would erase future reconciliation and could lose a result that was already accepted by the receiver or becomes readable later.

followups.question: Should all exceptions become unavailable?
followups.answer: No. Definite unauthorized scope, identity conflicts and invalid immutable source relationships need explicit rejection or step failure. Treating those as temporary can hide security or corruption defects and encourage repeated unsafe work.

questions.watch_for: Availability is not content validity; interruption must preserve completed row truth and prevent new rows after close.

evidence.label: Between-row proceed checks and commit boundary

questions.title: Refresh without rewriting history
questions.question: What does an applicability refresh command change, and why does replay happen before new reads?
answer: A refresh appends a separately versioned observation for one exact source result, with an explicit stable command ID and expected local metadata revision. It first looks up that command. An equal semantic replay returns its original receipt before fresh source/case reads or capacity checks; changing the target or expected revision conflicts. Otherwise the same retry could report a different answer merely because the world changed.

For a new command, the refresher validates the source event, original issuance and historical request/result/evidence. It separately observes current execution and current case state, then commits a bounded draft through local compare-and-set. That CAS orders derived metadata only; it does not make the P1 execution, host clock and case reads atomic. The returned receipt retains separate as-of fields and witnesses.

Invalidation is evidence-based. A retained higher revision, changed attempt or cancellation witness must not be revived by a later stale or unavailable read. An unavailable-only observation can recover when a later verified read establishes the missing information. Old grant lease expiry must not erase historical eligible result truth. A new refresh never grants delivery, action or consent permission.

followups.question: Why use expected local revision if source reads are non-atomic?
followups.answer: It prevents two refresh writers from silently overwriting one another's derived metadata order. It deliberately does not claim source consistency beyond the recorded observations. Those are different problems and require different authority boundaries.

followups.question: What happens after an uncertain refresh commit?
followups.answer: Perform one exact lookup by the original command and validate its target/revision. If absent or unreadable, preserve acknowledgement_unknown; do not submit another write. A definite CAS conflict likewise keeps its original meaning unless that exact command receipt proves success.

questions.watch_for: Refresh CAS orders metadata only; it cannot refresh the world atomically or authorize an action.

evidence.label: Replay before fresh reads or capacity
Source validation and exact commit reconciliation
Retained invalidation cannot revive from stale reads

questions.title: Hide display without deleting protection
questions.question: Why does hiding a result use a tombstone instead of deleting its projection and receipts?
answer: Display retention and effect protection have different lifetimes. A user or operator may no longer need a result card, but the system still needs original work, command, result, delivery and processing identities to reject replay conflicts and explain past effects. P3 therefore uses permanent presentation tombstones while retaining the original projection, refresh commands and ACKs for the profile lifetime.

Hiding changes neither refresh revision nor source identity, and it reclaims no protected capacity. It must not filter unresolved processing events: an invisible possible delivery may still need reconciliation. Authenticated original inspection and exact command replay remain available after hiding and at capacity. These details make display-window behavior safe rather than turning a UI cleanup action into an accidental idempotency reset.

The engineering cost is retained storage and explicit capacity planning. Before any real deletion mechanism is added, define replay horizons, protected tombstones, backup/restore behavior and how old commands are rejected after compaction. Business deadline expiry is not a substitute for a replay-retention policy. A small local profile can choose lifetime retention honestly; production needs a measured storage and recovery design.

followups.question: Can a display TTL free room for new accepted work?
followups.answer: Not under this contract. Accepted-work and protected identity capacity are separate from visible card count. Reclaiming one by hiding the other would permit old commands or effects to be accepted again without a defined replay horizon.

followups.question: How do you test hiding safely?
followups.answer: Assert the card disappears from display while original inspect/replay, projection bytes, ACK identities, refresh revision and authoritative receipts remain unchanged. Keep an unresolved possible-delivery event hidden and verify processing still sees it without retrying accept.

questions.watch_for: Deleting visible history is not safe deletion of replay, receipt or effect identities.

evidence.label: Display hide preserves original reads and replay

questions.title: Bind work to the original channel input
questions.question: What problem does the origin-bound policy v3 envelope solve beyond a delegation ID?
answer: A conversation can contain multiple inputs with identical text or generated policy requests. A caller-selected correlation ID does not prove which durable P2 input caused a particular accepted delegation. The v3 envelope binds the P2 profile ID, original operation UUID, input receipt UUID, canonical input digest and byte length to the nested fixed-policy request.

The original scoped operation selects the P1 key deterministically as p2_ plus the operation UUID's hexadecimal form. The outer fingerprint includes the complete origin and nested logical request while excluding changing wire-attempt correlation. This ensures two source inputs cannot collapse accidentally just because the model produced the same request, and a retry cannot relabel an existing operation with a different source receipt or payload.

The nested specialist contract remains fixed-policy v2. The explicit ChannelPolicyRunner adapter verifies the original source records, invokes the v2 specialist under a P1-issued attempt, and wraps the validated result in the v3 durable envelope. Source provenance is application-bound metadata; it does not itself authorize execution, delivery or mutation. Tests verify original outer bytes survive inner transport and that changed source records reject before invocation.

followups.question: Why not fingerprint only the transcript?
followups.answer: Identical transcript bytes can be separate legitimate inputs, while the same original input can be retransmitted. The stable operation and retained receipt distinguish those cases; the payload digest then detects changed content under that original identity.

followups.question: Can the specialist choose another origin?
followups.answer: No. The specialist receives the nested v2 computation request. Trusted application composition retains and validates the outer origin, and wraps only the matched validated result. Origin fields are not model-selected tool permissions.

questions.watch_for: A correlation ID or repeated text does not prove original-input ownership.

evidence.label: Outer v3 bytes survive nested v2 transport

questions.title: Preserve the first accepted origin winner
questions.question: Why does ChannelPolicyCoordinator expose both submit and accept?
answer: submit preserves exact logical matching for callers that mean to submit one immutable proposal. accept is the explicit original-channel-input path: an already accepted operation returns its first validated origin winner even if generated proposal details such as deadline or source configuration have changed. It never renews the retained proposal or executes work merely because it returns a record.

The distinction handles reconnect and ambiguous acknowledgement safely. A fresh process may regenerate a proposal for the same original P2 operation after time has moved on. It must discover the original accepted bytes instead of extending the deadline or selecting today's policy source. Origin identity and stable route fields still must match; changing profile, receipt, payload digest/length, case, revision or conversation conflicts rather than creating an alternate key.

For a genuinely new acceptance, the P1 created=true record must match the complete submitted canonical bytes, including attempt metadata. A first-winner recovery policy cannot excuse a port returning a different valid proposal on creation. Concurrent misses are reconciled to one original record, and an unknown lookup stays unknown without a second submit. This is a precise replay contract, not generic last-write-wins behavior.

followups.question: Does accept ignore changed customer intent?
followups.answer: No. It is selected only for replay of the same retained source operation, with exact stable origin and route bindings. A new customer input or case revision requires its own accepted operation; replay must not rewrite the old operation to represent it.

followups.question: Why validate created=true bytes more strictly?
followups.answer: Creation is the only moment the submitted proposal becomes authoritative. A substituted but structurally valid record would bind the caller to different deadline, evidence or attempt bytes. Replays can return the original winner; creation must prove it accepted this exact proposal.

questions.watch_for: First-origin replay does not renew deadlines, replace evidence or turn a new proposal into the old command.

evidence.label: Explicit exact submit and first-origin accept facades
Changed generated proposal versus exact stable origin

questions.title: Keep the conversation responsive
questions.question: How does the native policy application let a useful conversation continue while a specialist is held?
answer: NativePolicyApplication is a small bounded composition around an already configured read-only policy request. Its first tool call durably accepts work, owns one runner task and publishes a silent pending update only after acceptance. The run remains shielded from cancellation of the SDK waiter. An independent bounded read lane can inspect the original result while the specialist is held, so UI observation does not require starting another run.

The application returns a compact closed observation containing original bindings, work/attempt/result state, applicability, tool-waiter status and a non-atomic as-of marker. It does not expose arbitrary case selectors or a mutation tool. Repeated evaluation inspects the original identity; it is deliberately not an autonomous resume/retry endpoint. Tests distinguish a wrapper task that returned from actual pending ownership in injected ports.

The standalone I18B qualification uses actual RTC text with separate source/installed backend and browser assertions. It does not by itself qualify microphones, STT, TTS, P2 durable input or physical playback. The later joined showcase composes additional P2/P1/P3 behavior and has its own provider and scripted evidence. Keep those evidence boundaries separate when demonstrating responsiveness.

followups.question: Why reserve a read lane separately?
followups.answer: A status card should not deadlock behind the long-running evaluation it needs to observe. The lane is still finite and owned through actual settlement, preventing repeated browser polls from creating unbounded work while the specialist remains blocked.

followups.question: Why does repeated evaluate not start a new run?
followups.answer: The native facade is configured for one original operation. It offers stable inspection after waiter loss without guessing whether another attempt is safe. A separate explicit recovery command must obtain new P1 issuance authority under the recovery contract.

questions.watch_for: A pending progress event is not durable acceptance until acceptance happened, and RTC text is not audio qualification.

evidence.label: Accept before pending and one owned runner task
Held-run progress and reserved read assertions

questions.title: Treat images as untrusted evidence
questions.question: What protections exist around booking screenshot extraction?
answer: The document capability accepts one configured immutable PNG reference and produces four ordered structured fields with explicit complete, missing or ambiguous states and region evidence. It never accepts arbitrary URLs as authority or grants tools from image text. The source is scoped and digest-bound before decoding, and the extractor's output is reparsed and matched to the exact request.

The decoder bounds encoded bytes at 2 MiB, dimensions at 2048 by 2048 and total pixels at 4,194,304. It validates signature/header identity before creating a fixed worker module with an empty environment, no inherited execArgv and explicit worker memory limits. Expensive PNG validation runs off the event loop, and owned worker lifetime is observed through exit rather than assuming abort means termination.

These are safety and structural controls, not proof that extracted text matches the image. The tests use a separate literal image oracle to demonstrate that a schema-valid wrong value or region can still be factually wrong. Adversarial text remains inert data, and missing or ambiguous fields request clarification. General real-model OCR quality and integrated durable image execution are separate capabilities, not established by this scripted HTTP fixture.

followups.question: Why validate dimensions before decode?
followups.answer: Compressed byte size alone does not bound decompressed memory or CPU. Header dimensions and pixel ceilings reject oversized expansion before uncontrolled decoding, while the fixed worker provides another bounded lifetime and isolates expensive processing from conversational event-loop work.

followups.question: Can a highlighted phrase in the image authorize a refund?
followups.answer: No. Image content is untrusted evidence, even if it resembles a system instruction or says a customer approved. Only trusted controller input and the case authority's exact confirmation contract can authorize a business mutation.

questions.watch_for: Image format validity, field schema validity and factual extraction quality are three different claims.

evidence.label: Encoded size, dimensions and fixed empty-environment worker
Scoped image evaluation and provider ownership

questions.title: Keep image execution outside policy authority
questions.question: Why can't a valid document extraction result be passed into the existing durable policy runner?
answer: The durable P1 WorkPayload operation currently supports policy work under explicit supported codecs. The separate document HTTP capability has its own request/result schema, evidence model and resource requirements. Successful HTTP extraction therefore establishes only that bounded read-only document contract; it does not create P1 execution, projection, delivery or action compatibility.

Passing an image result through the policy runner would silently change persisted semantics, retained byte assumptions and downstream validation. P3 instead exposes a distinct DocumentSpecialistClient path that parses and matches document results without pretending they are policy execution records. The fixed-policy v2 and origin-bound v3 facades likewise opt into their exact schema behavior instead of changing the v1 default.

A future durable document extension needs an explicit versioned P1 operation contract, migration/compatibility plan, accepted evidence retention policy, result eligibility semantics and downstream consumers that understand the new bytes. It also needs image-worker crash/recovery and installed artifact tests. Reusing shared authenticated HTTP transport is valuable, but transport reuse must not be mistaken for supported durable orchestration.

followups.question: Is separating clients unnecessary API complexity?
followups.answer: Separate typed facades make unsupported combinations difficult to express and preserve existing defaults. Shared internal transport and codecs can reduce implementation duplication while public interfaces keep the meaning of accepted work and recorded results explicit.

followups.question: Could you store an opaque image result body in P1 anyway?
followups.answer: The storage ability to hold bytes does not authorize a new business operation. Its public payload contract, replay semantics, limits and consumers must explicitly support those bytes; otherwise the system can retain data that downstream code misinterprets or cannot safely reconcile.

questions.watch_for: Shared transport is not shared durable capability, and opaque storage is not an authority extension.

evidence.label: Separate document invocation is not a P1 policy result
Explicit schema3 runner with nested v2 transport
Durable policy operation excludes image results

questions.title: Recover through explicit original identities
questions.question: What exactly is demonstrated by the P3 process-recovery gate?
answer: The gate kills owned specialist/coordinator processes at explicit boundaries and restarts fresh consumers that inspect P1's retained authority. It includes original issuance replay with no invocation, a premature new command rejected until authority lease eligibility, and a separately supplied new eligible command that makes useful progress. Recovery does not add a timer-driven scheduler or an in-memory queue that owns accepted work.

Other cuts distinguish result precommit rollback from postcommit original bytes and feed truth, possible delivery before a receipt from receiver commitment, and action commitment from supplier application. Fresh processes reconcile exact work, attempt, request/result digests, receiver receipts and action confirmations. Independent histories join those identities; summary counts alone cannot prove no reinvocation or no physical reapply.

The selected recovery evidence is stronger than a mock restart because the parent owns and verifies the killed processes and SQL waiter relationships. It is still bounded local qualification for declared schedules. It does not establish general autonomous recovery, multi-region failover or remote-stop guarantees. State the demonstrated cuts and keep untested release scenarios visibly pending.

followups.question: What if the coordinator dies immediately after issue and before HTTP?
followups.answer: Original-command replay remains lookup-only because the restart cannot prove whether HTTP began. After P1 observes lease expiry, a caller can supply a new command that actually creates a new issuance. The accepted request and original attempt history remain intact.

followups.question: Why inspect actual supplier calls after recovery?
followups.answer: A logical idempotency receipt can hide duplicate physical requests. Independent call identities and every apply attempt show whether recovery actually reissued a side effect, while the authoritative receipt joins prove which original command the effect belongs to.

questions.watch_for: A restart demonstration qualifies its declared fault cuts; it is not an autonomous or globally available workflow service.

evidence.label: Original replay and useful current progress

questions.title: Close resources in dependency order
questions.question: What does cleanup_incomplete mean, and how should the application close shared readers?
answer: cleanup_incomplete means the component has not established that all owned operations and resources settled within its cleanup budget. It is not a successful shutdown with an inconvenient log message. Calls that already crossed write or external boundaries retain their observers; abandoned preflight calls are prevented from starting new writes. Close can be retried against retained ownership after the underlying work settles.

Lifecycle ownership is explicit. A completion facade owns its injected P1 delivery/action client and receiver, while the application owns shared result inspectors and case readers. Independent resources in the same dependency tier can close concurrently, but the application must observe successful closure of dependents before closing the shared readers they may still use. Otherwise a late receipt reconciliation fails because shutdown removed its dependency first.

NativePolicyApplication attempts coordinator and runner close independently with gather(return_exceptions=True), then checks the actual run/read reservations and pending port counts. It does not wait on a blocked wrapper before even asking other owners to close. The same principle applies to test tooling: do not delete schemas or private supplier files until every owned child is verified reaped. A stopped waiter is weaker evidence than an exited process or closed socket.

followups.question: Why retain the failed close task?
followups.answer: Its actual work may still be running and must remain observed. A retry should inspect or continue that owned closure, not spawn an unrelated cleanup path that loses the original resource identity. A completed failed close may be replaced deliberately while retaining the underlying owners.

followups.question: Should shutdown cancel a database write?
followups.answer: It may stop waiting within a bounded budget, but cannot assume the write rolled back. Preserve exact operation identity and observer ownership for reconciliation, and prevent new preflight writes after close begins.

questions.watch_for: A cancelled task or returned timeout does not prove threads, sockets, providers or child processes are gone.

evidence.label: Close abandons preflight, retains writes and observes actual tasks
Independent close attempts and actual ownership checks

questions.title: Deliver a package developers can consume
questions.question: How would you prove P3 is a reusable library rather than code that works only inside this checkout?
answer: The Python distribution declares its supported interpreter range, exact dependencies, src-layout package and py.typed marker. The TypeScript specialist has declared package exports and examples import those public surfaces. Public composition consumes P1's installed APIs rather than importing its storage internals or injecting sibling checkout paths into the consumer.

The standalone gate builds a fresh P1 dependency wheel and P3 wheel/sdist/rebuilt artifacts, packs the npm consumer, and executes isolated examples outside the checkout. Its default offline assertions require no SQL/settings; explicit lab assertions add real installed authority and failure behavior. Archive validation rejects traversal, links, unexpected payloads and changed dependency metadata so a passing import does not conceal accidental private files.

Developer experience includes an explicit scope mapping, separate confirmation input, clear resource ownership and fixed public error codes. A consumer must know which methods merely inspect, which may commit and what ambiguous acknowledgement means. Installed artifact evidence is necessary because source tests can accidentally import undeclared modules. It remains distinct from full platform or production-scale qualification, and no package-index publication is required for this local POC.

followups.question: Why test sdist rebuilds as well as wheels?
followups.answer: A wheel can work while the source distribution omits files or depends on checkout-only build inputs. Rebuilding and comparing maintained payload expectations verifies that a real downstream installer can reproduce the supported package boundary.

followups.question: Why does P3 depend on the P1 package if it is standalone?
followups.answer: Standalone means no undeclared sibling source imports or complete sibling service deployment. Depending on a declared installed narrow library contract is compatible with that goal. The public package contract should make required authority adapters and lifecycle ownership explicit.

questions.watch_for: Do not call a source-tree import an installed-consumer test or equate packaging with release qualification.

evidence.label: Declared Python distribution and exact dependency range

questions.title: Turn observations into safe diagnostics
questions.question: Which signals would you use to debug a stuck delegation without leaking user content?
answer: Start with distinct lifecycle counters and fixed operation/outcome/error codes: accepted input identity, issuance created/replayed, invoked, actual active work, waiter timeouts/cancellations, validated results, commit disposition, unknown delivery and processing gaps. Preserve enough scoped identity correlation in private evidence to join original authority records, while avoiding request bodies, tokens, image text or arbitrary remote exception strings in public logs.

P3's ContractError carries fixed safe codes. The coordinator logs only a closed event/operation/outcome/code vocabulary and contains logger failures, so telemetry cannot turn a committed acceptance into an apparent business failure. Transport metrics distinguish receiving framed HTTP bytes from validating capability semantics. A 200 response or healthy process does not prove a valid result, current applicability or useful user progress.

For a stuck case, inspect the original accepted record, issue command and grant, then the actual owned HTTP task, historical result, receiver marker/receipt and processing checkpoint independently. Do not repair the symptom by deleting the active slot or advancing an ACK watermark. Production alerting should focus on unresolved accepted work age and useful completion, with finite metric labels; this repository's selected diagnostics are not a production observability retention service.

followups.question: Why not put work IDs in metric labels?
followups.answer: Unbounded per-work labels create cardinality growth and memory cost. Keep aggregate metrics to finite dimensions and use appropriately protected traces or logs for identity correlation, with explicit sampling, retention and sanitization.

followups.question: What if the logger raises during a successful submit?
followups.answer: Contain and count the telemetry failure while preserving the actual accepted result. Retrying the business write because logging failed would turn an observability outage into a correctness problem. The caller still needs the original acceptance truth.

questions.watch_for: A successful HTTP exchange is not a validated result; telemetry failure must not rewrite business truth.

evidence.label: Closed diagnostic fields and contained logging failure

questions.title: Defend the remaining limits
questions.question: What would you say if an interviewer asked whether this delegation system is production-ready?
answer: I would describe a locally implemented reliability library with substantial selected evidence and explicit remaining release gaps. P3 has complete registered lab runners for three acceptance rows, P3-01, P3-03 and P3-11; the other fourteen full rows remain planned. Selected gates cover issued execution, exact completion, real process recovery, deadlines, images, fixed policy, native RTC text and origin-bound integration, but passing a task gate does not complete a charter row.

I would name the current limitations concretely: no autonomous P3 scheduler, no general multi-region or global-capacity claim, separate image HTTP without durable image execution, v1 projection/action consumers that do not automatically support v2/v3, and narrower native text evidence than audio/provider showcase evidence. The latest audit also retains low-severity issues such as starting-principal binding for status/cancel and native attempt-state behavior.

My next priorities would follow user impact: close known lifecycle/recovery gaps, define production identity and operator remediation contracts, expand complete acceptance runners, and measure fair native/local/remote behavior under declared loads. I would present AI assistance and personal contributions accurately, then demonstrate the boundary I can explain with code and evidence. Honest limitation analysis is part of engineering ownership, not a reason to discard the implementation.

followups.question: Which missing capability would you prioritize first?
followups.answer: Choose from the actual deployment risk: shutdown ordering and stranded accepted work are more urgent than adding new model capabilities. For P3 itself, preserve original-result truth and close lifecycle gaps, then qualify a complete integration scenario with actual useful progress and independent effect evidence.

followups.question: Does a recorded passing gate mean you reran it today?
followups.answer: No. The book is based on inspected source, tests and retained work-item reports. Historical evidence should be labelled as such. A current qualification requires running the declared lane successfully with its exact prerequisites and retaining new artifacts.

questions.watch_for: Do not sell selected local gates as complete release, production capacity, current reruns or personal authorship.

evidence.label: Three registered rows and remaining full acceptance

walkthrough.detail: A verified P2 prepared operation supplies profile, operation, input receipt, digest and length. ChannelPolicyCoordinator accepts one origin-bound canonical request through P1; acknowledgement loss looks up the original operation key.
The explicit runner asks P1 for an issued owner/epoch/lease grant. Only a newly created issuance plus the exact fresh running observation can begin HTTP. Original issue replay is lookup only.

The authenticated TypeScript service validates scope, per-operation grants, evidence and finite capacity. It evaluates fixed policy from immutable sources. No specialist tool can mutate bookings or send notifications.

The runner verifies schema, correlation and factual support, then records the exact result through P1. Late or cancelled results may remain historical with their P1 disposition. Current applicability is a separate non-atomic case observation.

P1 retains one original receiver/recipient/result intent. Only a created begin permits accept; later possible deliveries use find only. An accepted receiver receipt is neither carrier delivery nor human acknowledgement.

Branch to the separate original v1 compatibility path for guarded action. It receives exact human Confirmation and uses the public atomic P1 guard. Origin-bound v3 has its own explicit delivery path; v2/v3 do not flow through the v1 action/projector adapter.

Across supported paths, fresh processes inspect original identities and receipts. In the original v1 processing path, an unresolved possible send remains unknown and unACKed while a separate scan cursor permits later progress. Actual owners must settle and children must be reaped before cleanup.

limits: P3-01, P3-03 and P3-11 have registered complete lab runners; fourteen other full charter rows remain planned.
No autonomous P3 retry/recovery scheduler is introduced. New execution after an expired lease requires an explicit caller command and a newly created P1 issuance.
The standalone document HTTP capability is not supported by the existing durable policy runner, projection, delivery or action path.
Original v1 projector and guarded action consumers must not be presented as fixed-policy v2 or origin-bound v3 consumers. The latest audit records v2/v3 quarantine in the v1 projector.
I18B RTC text qualification does not establish physical microphone, STT/TTS, P2 native intake or playback. Later joined showcase evidence has its own scope.
The fixed-policy specialist is deterministic synthetic business logic; producer metadata uses null model identity and does not establish real-model reasoning quality.
Current local authorization has explicit finite principals and per-operation scopes. The latest audit records that status/cancel are not bound to the principal that started the active attempt.
Private process-kill, database and installed artifact evidence is historical, bounded qualification. This interview-book review did not run those lanes or invoke providers.

chapters.title: P3 Code decisions at the specialist boundary
chapters.subtitle: Sixteen source-first P3 defenses
intro: These cards begin with small real source slices, then ask what would break if a tempting simplification were made. The goal is to explain the contract and the failing schedule from actual implementation and test assertions, not memorize broad architecture language.

Each mechanism describes current code. Alternatives are explicitly marked as inferred trade-offs unless the repository records the decision or fix. Challenge sections identify observed test scenarios or documented repairs; proposed future work is labelled separately. The review did not edit application code or rerun database, browser, package or provider gates.

The P1 result-feed card is included because P3 consumes that public authority. P1 storage internals are evidence for understanding the producer guarantee, not an import path for P3 applications. Book IDs D3 are distinct from charter acceptance and implementation task IDs.

concepts.title: Read the predicate as a contract
concepts.body: Explain why the branch uses exact type, exact owner, created=true or exact receipt identity. Then identify the independent assertion that fails when the predicate is weakened.

concepts.title: Name the phase before promising cancellation
concepts.body: Preflight, possible durable write, possible external call and known result have different cleanup and recovery semantics. Waiter timeout alone decides none of the later facts.

concepts.title: Separate history from fresh permission
concepts.body: Original bytes and receipts remain facts after expiry, cancellation, hiding or a source outage. Fresh invocation, disclosure, delivery and action each retain their own admission contract.

concepts.title: Count actual work
concepts.body: Bounds must include wrapped pages, copied image bytes, decoded expansion, live threads, workers and observer notices. A returned promise or a hidden UI card does not automatically release the corresponding resource or identity.

questions.title: Reject ambiguous JSON before making a typed value
questions.question: Why use exact primitive checks and custom JSON hooks instead of accepting whatever json.loads returns?
answer: The decoder preserves duplicate-key evidence through object_pairs_hook instead of letting ordinary dict construction silently keep the last value. Its integer parser rejects negative zero, oversized lexical forms and values outside JavaScript's safe integer range. Separate float and constant hooks reject fractions, exponent notation and nonfinite constants. The typed integer helper also uses type(value) is int, so True cannot become a revision or byte length.

These choices establish one deliberately restricted cross-language meaning before canonical bytes or fingerprints are computed. The surrounding decoder bounds raw bytes and nesting first; canonicalization bounds the copied tree. This is not a general-purpose JSON compatibility layer. A caller receives a fixed contract error rather than a normalized request whose authority-bearing fields might mean something different in the other language.
questions.alternatives: Inferred trade-off: permissive JSON plus a schema validator is simpler and friendlier to generic producers. Here it would first discard duplicate-key evidence and could normalize distinct numeric forms differently. The closed wire protocol pays compatibility cost for deterministic rejection and explicit version evolution.
questions.counterfactual: Replace object_pairs_hook with the default parser and accept a payload containing duplicate scope or revision keys. One implementation can silently select a different value, while the original ambiguous bytes become impossible to inspect after projection.

challenge.symptom: A request appears valid in one language but fails or changes identity in the other, or a boolean passes as an integer. These are protocol-boundary symptoms rather than model-quality problems.
challenge.diagnosis: Inspect the raw bytes and parse phase before comparing typed objects. Ordinary parsing may already have removed duplicate keys, and Python numeric subtyping can make an isinstance check more permissive than intended.
challenge.handling: Existing handling uses duplicate-key, number and exact-type validators with shared invalid fixtures. Any future support for decimal input should be a defined new contract, not a local coercion added to one language.

followups.question: Why reject 1.0 when it equals 1 mathematically?
followups.answer: The selected protocol admits integers, not every numerically equivalent JSON spelling. Rejecting decimal and exponent forms keeps both producers on the same finite representation policy. If wider numeric compatibility is needed, specify and test its canonical form explicitly.

followups.question: Does the digest make duplicate keys harmless?
followups.answer: No. A digest identifies chosen bytes or normalized data; it does not choose a safe interpretation of ambiguous input. Reject the ambiguity before projecting into a dict or deriving semantic identity from a parser-selected winner.

followups.question: Why is isinstance(value, int) insufficient?
followups.answer: Python booleans are integer subclasses. Exact type checks preserve a distinction the wire contract actually requires, such as byte_length=true being invalid even if it compares equal to one. Static annotations do not enforce this at runtime.

questions.watch_for: Canonicalization must not erase evidence that the original request was ambiguous.

test.name: test_shared_invalid_contract_match_and_factual_lanes_have_fixed_codes
test.assertion: The shared inventory passes actual duplicate-root, duplicate-nested, fraction, exponent and negative-zero bytes to the public parser and checks exact fixed error codes. The boolean evidence-length test separately rejects a typed True value.

evidence.label: Duplicate and number hooks installed before projection
Actual duplicate and numeric invalid fixtures

questions.title: Keep logical identity stable across transport attempts
questions.question: Why does logical_fingerprint exclude attempt while still binding deadline, route and evidence?
answer: The logical fingerprint removes only the attempt object and the fingerprint itself, then hashes canonical immutable request semantics. A retry attempt can therefore carry new correlation without creating a new customer request. Scope, case, revision, evidence, context, deadline and conversation route still participate; changing any of them under the same delegation identity is a conflict.

Result matching adds the exact transport attempt back into its checks. Equal logical fingerprints do not permit attempt A's response to satisfy attempt B. The coordinator preserves the first accepted full bytes, and the runner replaces wire correlation only from a P1-issued grant. This separates three meanings that are easy to collapse: accepted business input, one authorized execution attempt and one result produced for that attempt.
questions.alternatives: Inferred trade-off: hashing the whole wire request is easy, but every retry would become a new logical operation. Hashing only the delegation ID is stable but misses changed content. The implemented exclusion list is narrow and makes future semantic fields binding by default.
questions.counterfactual: Exclude deadline or result_route as additional transport metadata. A replay could then renew an expired business horizon or redirect an original result while still presenting the old logical fingerprint as proof of equal accepted work.

challenge.symptom: A retry either creates duplicate logical work, or an old result is accepted for a different execution attempt. Both can appear harmless when only happy-path IDs are logged.
challenge.diagnosis: Compare the logical fingerprint separately from the exact attempt fields. Check which fields the exclusion set removes and whether the receiving result matcher verifies the issued attempt rather than the caller-proposed attempt.
challenge.handling: Existing tests preserve logical identity across attempt changes, reject the old response against the new attempt and require route, revision, source and deadline changes to alter identity. Broader semantic deduplication remains an advisory product decision.

followups.question: Why include the original deadline?
followups.answer: The deadline is part of the accepted service obligation and replay horizon for execution eligibility. Silently changing it would renew authority under an old command. A new attempt may reuse the original request, but it cannot rewrite that obligation.

followups.question: Why not let the specialist choose the next attempt?
followups.answer: The specialist can echo correlation, but P1 issues the authoritative grant. A proposed wire attempt is not execution permission. Only the runner maps that stored grant into transport metadata and later validates the response against it.

followups.question: Can equal text imply equal logical identity?
followups.answer: No. Two accepted channel inputs can contain identical text while representing separate user actions. Conversely, one original input may be retransmitted. Stable scoped operation identity plus exact canonical semantics distinguishes replay from a new accepted request.

questions.watch_for: Equal logical identity is not equal transport attempt, current permission or proof of source ownership.

test.name: test_attempt_retry_keeps_logical_identity_but_result_matches_exact_attempt
test.assertion: The test changes attempt correlation and asserts an unchanged fingerprint and duplicate classification. It then proves the old response fails exact matching, while a response explicitly bound to the new attempt succeeds.

evidence.label: Deadline, source and route remain identity-bearing

questions.title: Validate factual support before returning expired
questions.question: Why is the expired return after the factual checks in TypeScript verifyPolicyFacts?
answer: matchResult establishes correlation and computes timeliness, but an expired classification does not excuse unsupported content. verifyPolicyFacts first resolves the exact policy source, checks its version and digest, verifies the expected rule witness and recomputes the supported conclusion. Only after those checks can it return expired for a valid historical response.

The placement fixes an actual cross-language parity defect recorded in the audit: TypeScript previously let a late wrong answer escape as merely expired while Python rejected its facts. Historical results remain available to inspection and reconciliation, so false content must not gain credibility by arriving late. The fixed-policy v2 verifier follows the same separation. Time determines permitted use; it does not turn incorrect source claims into valid history.
questions.alternatives: Documented correction with inferred trade-off: returning early on expiry saves validation work and looks like sensible deadline handling. It also conflates unusable-now with factually-supported. The implementation accepts small bounded verification cost to keep historical truth and cross-language error semantics consistent.
questions.counterfactual: Move if (applicability === expired) return expired above the source and conclusion checks. The exact same late false result would become an ordinary timing outcome in TypeScript while remaining unsupported_facts in Python.

challenge.symptom: A factually wrong result is classified as expired by one consumer and rejected by another. The discrepancy appears only when the response crosses the deadline, so on-time fixtures can miss it.
challenge.diagnosis: Trace each return in the verifier. Separate correlation matching, exact source resolution, conclusion validation and temporal classification. Check whether any early expiry branch bypasses the evidence or boolean comparison.
challenge.handling: Existing handling places expiry after factual checks and adds a regression using the same late timestamp for both a wrong and a valid result. It does not claim that arbitrary model prose can be independently verified.

followups.question: Why retain a valid late result at all?
followups.answer: The result can be useful historical evidence about what computation returned, even when it cannot authorize new work. Preserve its exact identity, content and disposition, then let current applicability and operation guards determine what may happen next.

followups.question: Should a late malformed response consume result capacity?
followups.answer: The public runner rejects invalid result bytes before completion. A result must first pass the supported structural and factual contract to enter this history path. Late is a disposition of validated content, not an alternative parser success state.

followups.question: Does producer completed_at restore eligibility?
followups.answer: No. It is metadata from another clock and producer. P1 evaluates time, lease and cancellation at its protected commit, while P3 validates facts separately. Neither a claimed early completion nor a late receipt can bypass those boundaries.

questions.watch_for: A deadline failure does not grant permission to skip factual validation.

test.name: rejects unsupported facts before reporting expiry, in the same order as Python
test.assertion: One late timestamp is used with a flipped eligibility conclusion and a valid conclusion. The independent assertions require unsupported_facts for the former and expired for the latter, exposing the old early-return defect.

evidence.label: Python parity assertion for the same late factual distinction

questions.title: Treat issuance as a one-call capability
questions.question: Why return without invoking on created=false, then obtain a second exact observation on created=true?
answer: created=false means this issue command already has a retained grant. The original caller may have invoked before losing its acknowledgement, so replay returns an observation and no new HTTP call. Even reconciliation of an unknown issue acknowledgement cannot manufacture the missing knowledge that the first invocation did not happen.

A newly created issuance is necessary but the runner still obtains a fresh current observation before crossing into HTTP. It requires running state, no cancellation and the exact current grant, including owner and epoch; the immediately following condition checks lease time too. This catches cancellation or supersession between issue and transport. It remains a preflight, not a remote revocation fence: once read-only I/O starts, late result handling and P1 completion disposition preserve what actually returns.
questions.alternatives: Inferred trade-off: invoke whenever issue returns a grant is simpler and avoids a conservatively unused attempt after a crash. It also duplicates calls after acknowledgement loss. The extra observation costs a read but catches known changes before external work without inventing distributed cancellation.
questions.counterfactual: Delete the created=false return or reuse the pre-issue observation. The first edit reinvokes an original command after transport loss; the second starts HTTP even when the test cancels the work immediately after issuing its grant.

challenge.symptom: An acknowledgement retry calls the specialist twice, or work cancelled immediately after issuance still starts HTTP. A stored grant exists in both cases, so checking only for non-null issuance does not distinguish them.
